newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia foreign minister may be set to go - source.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia foreign minister may be set to go - source.

text.p: Sources close to Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler, under strong attack from the opposition, said he might resign later on Thursday.
The foreign ministry would neither confirm nor deny the sources' comments.
Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek has said Thaler is seriously considering resigning for personal reasons and in the face of continuing opposition attacks, which Drnovsek judged unfounded.

The main opposition party, the Social Democrats, last week called for a parliamentary debate on the government's effectiveness. The debate, which is expected to take place in September, could lead to a no-confidence vote.

Thaler's performance is likely to be at the centre of the debate. The opposition has attacked him over amendments to the constitution allowing foreigners to buy land. The changes were necessary as part of Slovenia's drive to join the EU.
Thaler, 35, is a member of Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats. He has held his post since late February, when the new government was formed following November general elections.

He held the same position for over a year in the previous government but was ousted in May 1996 by a parliamentary no-confidence vote. Then he stood accused of failing Slovenia in the way he negotiated associate EU membership.
His resignation would have to be approved by parliament. Therefore, if he resigned, Thaler would probably stay in his post until September when parliament reassembles after the summer recess.
